# 05 ZEAROX — voicing round (Batch 3B, the wreck and chop set)

*Generated by tests/voicing/batch03b.py. Level reading: RMS over the note-on region of the kick phrase (phrase m: 11 hits x 150 ms); matched to the bank reference (-18.0 dBFS RMS) by VOLUME; phrase (b)'s reading is in the table too. Every change is before -> after under the echo rule. WAVs are on the listen/batch-03b-chapter1-wreck-and-chop branch only.*

**Recommended: B blown** - MONO, three layers in one voice. THE SUB: OSC 1 pulse at the note's own pitch (LEVEL 90); the original was this plus a saw an octave down and nothing else (sub only: -23.5 dBFS on the kick phrase at VOLUME 100, -10.9 dB of it left after a 100 Hz high-pass, no energy above 400 Hz). THE BODY: OSC 2 saw an octave UP (SEMI +12) at LEVEL 127, swept down by the filter envelope through ENV>O2 110 (+17 st at the strike, falling over FILTER DECAY 58 = 46 ms): the 808-style chirp, and it puts the pitch in the 60-400 Hz bands. THE CLICK: NOISE 50 through the same fast filter envelope (CUTOFF 65, ENV AMT 120, SUSTAIN 0, KEY TRK 20 so a low note is not darker than a high one). The amp is a drum's: attack 0.5 ms, DECAY 82 (= 299 ms), SUSTAIN 0, RELEASE 30. THE OVERLOAD: GROWL 104 (BIAS 72, TONE 64) and CHEW 127, HISS 0. Where the kick lives on the isolated A1 hit (share of the energy above 60 Hz in the click / body / tail windows): B 78 / 86 / 62 %, the original 38 / 21 / 10 %; the click window (0-10 ms) has 19 % of its energy above 400 Hz (the original: 0), the body window 51 % at 150-400 Hz and 27 % at 60-150 Hz, the true sub (under 60 Hz) 14 % of the body. On A0 the energy above 60 Hz is 93 / 86 / 63 % (click / body / tail) and on A2 96 / 100 / 100 %. The click is spectral, not a level spike: the first 5 ms of an A1 hit sit -1.0 dB against the body (the original: +2.0), and the hit reaches 90 % of its peak at 58 ms (the sub beating with the swept body); a click that spiked over the body would need a quieter body, which the -18.0 dBFS level over a 150 ms gate does not leave room for (README section 8). A small speaker that stops at 100 Hz keeps -2.6 dB of the kick phrase (the original -10.9). Level -18.0 dBFS on the kick phrase, -19.2 on phrase (b), peak -10.3 dBFS, crest 7.8 dB over the phrase; the first 30 ms of an A1 hit have a crest of 2.8 dB (GROWL 0 on this patch: 5.7; a sine is 3). Worst case 2753 host instr/sample (the original 1361): CHEW costs 768, GROWL 579. C puts the click first (click above 400 Hz: 13 % on A1, the sub down from 90 to 70), D is the tamer overload (GROWL 55: hit crest 5.8 dB, click above 400 Hz 0 % on A1).

## What to listen to

`*_kick.wav` is the one to judge: three isolated hits (A0, A1, A2) with a second of silence after each, then four hits a bar at 120 BPM. `*_riff.wav` / `*_stabs.wav` / `*_held.wav` are the pilot phrases (a MONO patch plays the last note of a chord; a kick held for 2.4 s decays by itself).
Listen for: whether A1 and A2 read as a kick and not as a bass note (the chirp and the click), whether A0 gives anything but air, how blown B is against D, and whether C's click is a click or a hiss. Play it on the small speaker.

*Notes.* Level is read on the note-on region of the kick phrase (11 hits x 150 ms), a short transient sound; crest factor over that region is in the table, and the crest of the first 30 ms of each hit is the overload reading (sine 3 dB, saw 4.8, a flattened wave lower). The band windows start at each hit's real onset (the host quantises note events to its blocks, so the sound begins up to a few ms either side of the nominal time).
'Small speaker' = a zero-phase 2nd-order high-pass at 60 / 100 Hz on the whole phrase: the level that remains against the unfiltered one. **Noise:** the voice NOISE goes through the filter and the amp envelope, so it stops with the note (B's isolated A1 hit is 60 dB down 62 ms after the key-up, the voice alone 18 ms); the TAPE hiss (HISS, 0 here) is
not gated: it comes up with CHEW, stays about 2 s after the last note and then fades (the HISS probe, dBFS right after the last note / at +2.4 s: HISS 32 -56 / -61, HISS 64 -50 / -54, HISS 96 -44 / -48; a hit is at -18). **CHEW at the top changes little in the numbers here:** with CHEW 0 / 127 the level reading moves -18.0 against -18.2 dBFS, the first-30-ms crest 2.3 -> 2.8 dB,
the click's share above 400 Hz 23 -> 19 %; the dropout probe (48 hits, 24 s, DROPS at its default 64) found 0 hits more than 3 dB under the median. What it adds that these numbers do not show (wow, flutter, head loss) is untested by ear. The flattening is GROWL's (the GROWL probe: crest 5.7 at 0, 3.4 at 76, 2.8 at 104). The sub is OSC 1 LEVEL (the O1_LVL probe: 50 -> 110 moves the energy under 60 Hz from 9 to 49 %, all at the same level reading after VOLUME).
**The tape's effect on A0:** a 27.5 Hz fundamental is inaudible on a small speaker whatever is done to it; what is heard on A0 is the swept body and the GROWL harmonics (energy above 60 Hz in the body window: 86 %).
